artifact: the ported response build against the published carrier
acceptance_test: elementwise comparison of the rebuilt response against the published one. The carrier pins do NOT check response values: the semantic identity digests input arrays and the resolved targets, and the stored response digest is self-consistent with whatever was built. A changed kernel therefore passes every loader check, so the loader is not the acceptance test and this comparison is.
reading: a faithful port at float64 round-off: the values move at 3.6e-16 absolute, 4.3e-11 of the peak element, on 98.5 percent of elements. The published carrier is NOT republished, because rebuilding it would move almost every element at that level for no gain -- it warm-loads in 0.04 s and nothing needs it rebuilt. The gain is for the NEXT build: the Green kernel is no longer the dominant cost, and the 117 s that remains is host work -- shapely section polygons, the per-circuit union and overlap attribution, and the input digests -- which is now the bottleneck to attack.
